issue_context.title: Live Streaming not working in Frontend if GENERIC Camera supports only UDP rtsp protocol
issue_context.body:
## The problem
I use a generic camera that provides an rtsp stream. I can see it in VLC.
But this stream is only working with UDP rtsp_transport.

When I configure my generic camera camera, I specify a stream_source, but stream cannot be displayed in Lovelace.

This same problem has been solved for Onvif camera [here](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/23094) by allowing to specify a stream_options.

Is it possible to fix it also for generic camera ?

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 
0.110.3

- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 
None

- Operating environment: 
Hassio

- Integration causing this issue: 
stream
generic_camera

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
```- platform: generic
      name: test_camera
      still_image_url: http://192.168.0.21:1234/image/jpeg.cgi
      stream_source: rtsp://username:password@192.168.0.21:554/play1.sdp
      username: username
      password: password
      verify_ssl: false
```

## Traceback/Error logs

```
2020-05-27 01:31:34 ERROR (stream_worker) [libav.rtsp] method SETUP failed: 461 Unsupported Transport

```
comments: Same issue here with a Yoosee Doorbell Camera.

There hasn't been any activity on this issue recently. Due to the high number of incoming GitHub notifications, we have to clean some of the old issues, as many of them have already been resolved with the latest updates.
Please make sure to update to the latest Home Assistant version and check if that solves the issue. Let us know if that works for you by adding a comment 👍
This issue has now been marked as stale and will be closed if no further activity occurs. Thank you for your contributions.
Can someone with the issue test if https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/46623 works?

review_comments: This looks equivalent to `self.stream_options[CONF_RTSP_TRANSPORT] = device_info[CONF_RTSP_TRANSPORT]`.  Is the double look up here serve another purpose?

Yeah it is equivalent. It's to decouple what we are using for in HA for `CONF_RTSP_TRANSPORT` from what pyav/ffmpeg uses as an input option. Both happen to be `rtsp_transport`. The code in `onvif` did not decouple these.
If we wanted to be anal, I guess we could decouple the values as well :-P

Makes sense.

Sorry also I just saw this was a draft.  I cam across it just looking at the review backlog and didn't notice.
